subject: Cobalt expansion: capability petition for customer-deterministic model affinity + soft cost cap
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Cobalt expansion: capability petition for customer-deterministic model affinity + soft cost cap

Team —

Quick context: Cobalt (enterprise, finance) is late-stage and just signaled procurement for an expanded contract (see attached SOW summary). Their legal/procurement team insists on two things before signature: 1) deterministic affinity so their regulated workloads always route to a pinned model variant (for auditability), and 2) an acceptable cost ceiling per 1M tokens for bursty periods (they want a soft cap and a technical fallback rather than a hard shutdown).

Key asks from Sales/CS: can Product/Eng evaluate whether we can deliver an MVP of "per-tenant deterministic model affinity" combined with a tunable soft cost cap (fallback to lower-cost model variant + throttled burst queue) within a 4–6 week window? Cobalt has committed to a procurement cutoff of 2027-06-25; they need either the technical assurance or a committed discount path if we can’t meet the timing.

Why this matters: this is a $2.4M ARR expansion; high strategic value (referenceable financial customer) and we get to harden tenancy/routing controls that other enterprise prospects have started asking about.

Proposed MVP (Sales-side suggestion):
- API flag + account-level routing rule to prefer pinned model variants (best-effort determinism for new sessions)
- A configurable soft cost cap per account that, when breached, routes to a pre-authorized fallback model and applies a temporary token-cost alert rather than hard-blocking requests
- Telemetry slice: per-account token counts, routing decisions, and a simple audit log export for compliance review

Attachments: COB_SOW_Summary.pdf, cobalt_usage_snapshot_20270610.csv

Asks: can Eng/Prod provide a feasibility read and a rough effort estimate by Monday EOD so I can update Cobalt and Procurement? If the ETA is >6 weeks we need to discuss commercial fallback (discount / extended trial + audit export).

Thanks —
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cobalt expansion: capability petition for customer-deterministic model affinity + soft cost cap

Vivek —

Thanks for the clear brief. Quick reactions from an engineering lens:
- Deterministic model affinity is doable as an opt-in routing policy, but true determinism across sessions requires careful session-keying and KV cache considerations. For an MVP we can provide a per-account "preferred model" setting that will be honored for new sessions; existing cached sessions may still land on previous nodes until TTLs expire.
- The soft cost cap behavior (route-to-fallback + alert) is relatively straightforward from a routing/feature-toggle side, but the challenge will be ensuring the fallback maintains acceptable latency and semantic quality for Cobalt's workflows. If they accept a lower-capacity variant with slightly degraded quality we can save a lot of work.

Estimate request: to get a reliable spike + small prototype (routing rule, fallback switch, basic telemetry) I'd expect: 3 engineering days for spike, 2–3 engineers 2–3 weeks for MVP implementation, 1 week for QA+docs. That assumes no major infra changes in the runtime affinity layer.

Questions for Sales/CS:
1) How strict is their audit requirement? Do they need per-request signature that ties model choice to an audited key, or is per-session audit log sufficient?
2) Are they willing to accept a documented fallback model in the SOW (they explicitly asked for auditability, which influences our acceptance criteria)?

I'll block time for a spike if Prod approves.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SW Eng, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cobalt expansion: capability petition for customer-deterministic model affinity + soft cost cap

Adding customer color from the CS thread and a quote from Elliot at Cobalt: "We need an auditable guarantee that regulated workloads always map to the same model variant — our auditors will flag any non-deterministic routing. If Redwood can provide a documented per-account affinity + an exportable audit trail, we'll sign. If not, we will need a commercial credit to cover audit remediation work."

Timeline constraints: procurement is pushing to sign by 2027-06-25 (they want the SLA and custom routing in the contract). Internal timeline ask from Cobalt: availability for pilot in production by 2027-07-15. They are explicit that the fallback plan must be spelled out in the SOW (what happens when cost cap triggers).

Operational constraints: Cobalt's usage is bursty (see csv). They will accept a documented fallback model with a 10–20% quality delta as long as we provide the audit export and a guaranteed gradual ramp back to the preferred model post-burst. They also prefer a control-plane UI toggle for CS to set affinity and cost cap thresholds (not mandatory for MVP, but a request).

If Product/Eng can commit to an MVP that meets the audit export + preferred-model routing for new sessions and a clear fallback flow, I will push procurement to extend the sign date target for any minor implementation lag, but they want the technical assurances this week.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Cobalt expansion: capability petition for customer-deterministic model affinity + soft cost cap

Appreciate the quick takes — here are pragmatic acceptance criteria and a commercial fallback proposal to keep procurement moving:

MVP acceptance criteria (Prod + CS):
- Per-account preferred-model flag honored for all NEW sessions (documented behavior and limitations around existing KV caches)
- Ability to export per-account routing decisions for any 24h window (CSV export, includes timestamp, chosen model, and request id)
- Soft cost cap control that triggers an automated route-to-fallback and generates an alert to CS + customer (no automatic hard-block)
- Fallback model defined in the SOW and acknowledged by Cobalt (will accept 10–20% quality delta)

Commercial fallback (if Eng needs >6 weeks):
- Sales offers a 12% one-time implementation credit applied to first-year invoices + guaranteed telemetry export delivered by the earlier of pilot start or 2027-08-01

Related HubSpot: https://hubspot.redwood/deals/COB-2027-1197 (I will update with these acceptance criteria after we confirm feasibility).

If Product/Eng can commit to the acceptance criteria with the timeline Marcus sketched (spike this week; MVP in 3–5 weeks), I will lock Procurement to the 6/25 signature date. Otherwise I will propose the implement-credit option in writing.

Thanks —
Vivek

High-level production estimate and next steps:

Estimate (rough):
- Spike (confirm feasibility, telemetry hooks, audit export format): 3 engineer-days (1 backend + 1 infra)
- MVP implementation: 3 weeks (routing policy + fallback switch + basic export endpoint + minimal UI toggles for CS)
- QA + docs + runbook: 4–7 days

Total ballpark: 4–5 weeks if we prioritize and avoid parallel larger infra refactors. If we can scope the audit export to a nightly CSV export (rather than streaming per-request audit logs) we can shave ~5 days.

Next steps:
1) Convert this thread into a formal feature request (FR-7842) with acceptance criteria from Vivek and timeline proposal.
2) Approve a 3-day spike (I will assign owners once FR is created).
3) Sales/CS to confirm whether the commercial fallback credit is acceptable if we miss the 6-week window.

I can take the FR through planning if Sales gives the green light for the spike.

—Kimberly
